advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] De-duplicate failures between the walk_packages loop body and _on_walk_error, and count onerror-reported modules in `attempted`, so a broken subpackage __init__ is reported once with an accurate pass tally.
evidence: scripts/check_import_walk.py:160: for info in pkgutil.walk_packages(root.__path__, prefix=prefix, onerror=_on_walk_error):
scripts/check_import_walk.py:152: def _on_walk_error(name: str) -> None:  (appends to failures but does not increment attempted)

ABSENCE: the synthetic broken_package fixture (tests/scripts/test_check_import_walk.py:100-113) breaks LEAF modules broken_a.py / sub/broken_b.py, never a subpackage __init__.py, so the double-report/onerror path is untested.
advisory.finding: A broken subpackage __init__.py is double-reported and skews the pass count: pkgutil.walk_packages yields the subpackage (imported and recorded as a failure in the loop body, incrementing `attempted`) and then re-imports it internally to descend, which fails and fires `_on_walk_error` — recording the SAME module a second time without incrementing `attempted`. `passed = total - len(failures) - len(skips)` can then be understated or negative.
scenarios: A subpackage's __init__.py raises ImportError (the exact 'subpackage import breakage' class cited in the docstring, cinderlike-faulty-yucker) — it is listed twice in the report and the 'passed' tally is wrong.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track seen module names in a set shared by the loop and _on_walk_error, skip re-recording an already-seen name, and increment `attempted` when onerror records a new module.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard against a None __doc__ when deriving the argparse description (e.g. `(__doc__ or '').splitlines()[0] if __doc__ else None`).
advisory.finding: `argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])` raises AttributeError when the module is run under `python -OO`, where `__doc__` is stripped to None.
scenarios: The check is invoked via `python -OO scripts/check_import_walk.py` (optimized bytecode with docstrings removed).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where an expected-optional module raises ModuleNotFoundError for its declared dep while that dep IS importable, asserting it is classified as a failure (guards the find_spec branch of _classify_package_failure).
evidence: scripts/check_import_walk.py:138-141: `and exc.name == entry.dep\n        and importlib.util.find_spec(entry.dep) is None`
docstring: 'Any other failure — or a failure while the dep IS installed — is a real failure.'
The two expected-optional tests (lines 128-147) cover only the absent-dep skip and the wrong-declared-name failure; neither reaches the find_spec guard as the deciding branch.
ABSENCE: no test constructs an EXPECTED_OPTIONAL entry whose dep raises ModuleNotFoundError while find_spec resolves the dep.
advisory.finding: The expected-optional classifier's 'dep IS installed => real failure' branch is untested. `_classify_package_failure` skips a module only when `importlib.util.find_spec(entry.dep) is None`; the docstring states 'a failure while the dep IS installed — is a real failure.' No test covers an EXPECTED_OPTIONAL module that raises ModuleNotFoundError for its declared dep while that dep is importable. `test_expected_optional_missing_dep_is_a_skip` uses an absent dep and `test_expected_optional_different_missing_name_is_a_failure` uses a wrong declared name (which fails at the `exc.name == entry.dep` check), so the `find_spec(...) is None` guard is never the deciding condition. A regression that dropped that guard would still pass all tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a broken_package variant whose module does `import <a-real-installed-module>` inside a try that re-raises `ModuleNotFoundError('<real-module>')`, declare it EXPECTED_OPTIONAL with dep=<real-module>, and assert it lands in failures (not skips).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct test of `--child`/`_import_one_script` asserting ambient sys.path stripping (a bare sibling import fails even when scripts dir would otherwise be on the path) and the spec-build-failure return code.
evidence: scripts/check_import_walk.py:180-186: `ambient = {"", str(Path.cwd()), str(SCRIPTS_DIR)}` ... `if spec is None or spec.loader is None: ... return 1`
ABSENCE: no test calls `walk.main(["--child", ...])` or `walk._import_one_script(...)`; TestMain only invokes `--leg scripts`.
The isolation claim in test_sibling_insert_cannot_mask_the_missing_one relies on subprocess separation but does not assert that the child strips its ambient path entries.
advisory.finding: The `--child` mode (`_import_one_script`) — which performs the ambient-sys.path stripping that IS the standalone-import isolation contract — is never invoked directly by a test. It is exercised only indirectly through `walk_scripts` subprocesses, so neither the stripping of `""`/cwd/SCRIPTS_DIR nor the spec-build-failure branch (`spec is None or spec.loader is None` -> return 1) has a direct assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call `walk.main(["--child", str(bridge_py)])` (or `_import_one_script`) directly and assert rc==1 with a bare-import target; add a case pointing --child at a non-importable path to cover the spec/loader-None branch.
